title: Cisco Secure Network Analytics Alarm Volume
exclusions: Covers alarms the Cisco Security Cloud SNA input writes as cisco:sna. Flow Collector exports and Enterprise Security notables are separate use cases.
evidence: Hourly alarm counts for 30 days, and a note when a staffed hour has zero alarms.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Raise a test alarm in the Stealthwatch Management Console. After the next input interval (default 300 seconds) the hour's alarms count increases by at least one.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Stop the SNA input. The following staffed hour shows zero alarms, and the silence alert fires.

dataSources: `index=cisco_sna sourcetype=cisco:sna` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Secure Network Analytics input. The user guide sets this sourcetype and index as the defaults and pulls alarms from the Manager API (`POST /report-builder/api/v1/reports/alarms`). The add-on publishes no field list, so this search counts events rather than reading undocumented alarm fields. Promotion severities documented on the input are All, Critical, Major, Minor, Trivial, and Info.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Secure Network Analytics input.

description: Counts Cisco Secure Network Analytics alarms per hour. The add-on writes them as cisco:sna and does not publish field names, so the search counts events instead of parsing severity or host.
value: SNA finds hosts that scan, hoard data, or beacon, including devices with no agent. A flat alarm count tells the SOC whether that feed is alive and whether tonight is louder than last week, which is the first check before anyone hunts a single alarm.
implementation: Enable the Secure Network Analytics input in Cisco Security Cloud (7404) into index=cisco_sna. Chart alarms per hour and alert when a staffed hour is empty.
visualization: Column chart of alarms per hour over 24 hours, with a single value for the latest hour.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Quiet networks** — a site with few internal hosts can have hours with no alarms. Compare with the same hour last week before paging.

2. **Input catch-up** — the first run reads back from the After setting (default 10 minutes ago is the steady state; a new input can backfill and spike one hour).

**Suppression:** alert only when the count is zero during staffed hours.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• A Stealthwatch Management Console account: host, domain id, username, and password, as the user guide lists under SNA credentials.
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_sna`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Secure Network Analytics card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_sna`.
• The input writes `cisco:sna`.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna" earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count as alarms
```

Understanding this SPL
• `timechart span=1h` counts events. The user guide does not publish alarm field names, so severity and host are not filtered.
• The default interval is 300 seconds, so each hour should contain several input runs.

Step 3 — Validate
• In the Stealthwatch Management Console open the alarm list for the same hour and compare the count with this panel. They will not match event-for-event if the input's After window and the console filter differ, but a console that shows alarms while Splunk shows zero means the input is down.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Secure Network Analytics and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• HTTP 401 in the input log: the SMC username, password, or domain id (tenant_id) is wrong.
• No events and the console has alarms: the SMC host is not reachable on HTTPS from the input host, or the index name on the input is not cisco_sna.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We count the network alarms Cisco raises each hour, so we notice when that feed goes quiet or suddenly gets much louder.
